reason: The claim reveals that this building's mismatched massing -- a 4-story east section, an 11-story main section, a 5-story set-back attic level, and 7-story tower -- is not an aesthetic accident but physical evidence of construction in three stages between 1912 and 1932, when it was built for The New York Times. That turns a visibly odd building into a legible record of its own phased construction history, changing how a walker reads its facade rather than just adding a date.
